query: Identify a processing route and property optimization strategy for a lightweight, multi-principal element alloy system. The goal is to achieve high density and hardness while ensuring resistance to high-temperature oxidation and aqueous corrosion. Request a hypothesis for the material composition and processing method, supporting evidence on phase stability, boundary conditions for the processing temperature, and a falsification experiment to test the mechanism of property enhancement.

generation.hypothesis: Optimizing the rotational speed of Stationary Friction Processing (SFP) to an intermediate value (e.g., 900 rpm) in an equimolar AlCoCrFeNi High Entropy Alloy will maximize the fraction of high-angle grain boundaries (HAGBs) and ultrafine grain size, thereby achieving a synergistic balance of high hardness and high-temperature oxidation resistance without the bimodal grain distribution or excessive HAGB reduction seen at extreme speeds.
generation.material_initial_state: Equimolar AlCoCrFeNi High Entropy Alloy in as-cast condition with coarse grains and a high fraction of high-angle grain boundaries (~87%).
generation.intervention: Apply Stationary Friction Processing (SFP) at an intermediate rotational speed (e.g., 900 rpm) for a fixed duration (5 min), positioned between the previously tested speeds of 400 rpm and 1800 rpm.
generation.conditions: Processing temperature controlled by the frictional heat generation at the specific rotational speed; post-processing microstructural analysis at ambient and elevated temperatures (up to 600 K).
generation.structural_mediator: Grain boundary character distribution, specifically the volume fraction of high-angle grain boundaries (HAGBs, θ > 15°) and the uniformity of the grain size distribution (elimination of bimodal structures).
generation.mechanism: Intermediate strain rates (rotational speeds) provide sufficient shear deformation to refine grains and increase HAGB density (enhancing strength/hardness via Hall-Petch) without inducing the severe texture or localized deformation bands that cause bimodal distributions and HAGB reduction observed at high speeds (1800 rpm). This optimized microstructure promotes the formation of a stable, protective Al-rich oxide layer, enhancing oxidation resistance.
generation.predicted_outcome: The intermediate speed sample will exhibit a higher fraction of HAGBs (>82%) and a more uniform ultrafine grain structure compared to the 1800 rpm sample, resulting in superior hardness retention at 600 K and improved oxidation resistance compared to both the as-cast and 1800 rpm samples, while avoiding the mechanical property degradation associated with bimodal grains.
generation.baseline: The 1800 rpm SFP sample, which shows superior grain refinement but suffers from a reduced HAGB fraction (~66%) and bimodal grain distribution, and the 400 rpm sample which has less refinement.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is bounded by the rotational speed range of 400–1800 rpm; speeds outside this range or significantly different dwell times may alter the deformation mechanism. The alloy composition is restricted to the equimolar AlCoCrFeNi system as per the available evidence.
generation.uncertainty: The evidence explicitly states that the optimal speed and the effect of intermediate speeds are unexplored (PMC9026100::rubric_gaps::001::7bfac530a0). It is uncertain whether the relationship between rotational speed, HAGB fraction, and oxidation resistance is monotonic or if a specific peak exists at an intermediate speed, or if the trade-off between grain refinement and HAGB preservation is non-linear.

falsification_experiment.design: Perform SFP on equimolar AlCoCrFeNi at 400, 900, and 1800 rpm for 5 minutes. Characterize the grain size distribution and HAGB fraction using EBSD. Measure hardness at 300 K and 600 K. Conduct cyclic oxidation tests at 800 K for 50 hours.
measurements: Grain size distribution uniformity (coefficient of variation)
Vickers hardness at 300 K and 600 K
Oxide layer thickness and composition after oxidation
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if the 900 rpm sample does not exhibit a higher HAGB fraction than the 1800 rpm sample (>66%) while maintaining a more uniform grain structure, OR if the hardness at 600 K and oxidation resistance of the 900 rpm sample are not superior to the 1800 rpm sample.

cited_evidence.text: Gap and lever. Type: limitation. Statement: The processing method (Stationary Friction Processing) was only tested at two specific rotational speeds (400 and 1800 rpm), leaving the optimal speed and the effect of intermediate speeds unexplored.. System: AlCoCrFeNi High Entropy Alloy. Lever: rotational speed of the processing tool. Quote: "The ultrafine-grain microstructure is obtained using stationary friction processing performed at two different rotational speeds, 400 and 1800 rpm, for 5 min duration."

Gap and lever. Type: tradeoff. Statement: Higher rotational speeds (1800 rpm) achieve superior grain refinement and oxidation resistance but result in a bimodal grain distribution and a significant reduction in the fraction of high-angle grain boundaries compared to lower speeds.. System: AlCoCrFeNi High Entropy Alloy. Lever: rotational speed (strain rate). Quote: "The fraction of high angle grain boundaries (HAGBs, θ > 15°) is reduced from nearly 87% for the as-cast sample to ∼82% and 66% for the SFP_400 and SFP_1800 samples, respectively."

Gap and lever. Type: future_work. Statement: The authors imply a need to extend these findings to other HEA systems and to investigate the mechanical properties of the processed samples under high-temperature conditions to ensure comprehensive material viability.. System: High Entropy Alloys (HEAs). Lever: alloy system composition and mechanical property testing. Quote: "Thus, there is a need to develop advanced materials with superior surface oxidation resistance and improved mechanical properties at high temperature."

Gap and lever. Type: tradeoff. Statement: Increasing temperature leads to higher corrosion rates and less stable surface oxide growth, despite the protective nature of the FCC phase.. System: AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 EHEA. Lever: temperature. Quote: "The I corr value increased with an increase in temperature for both alloys, indicating the high dissolution rate and relatively poor protective nature of their surface passivation layer."
